Book: 'Γ is a Dynkin diagram if the quadratic form on ℝⁿ with matrix A is positive definite.' Lean defines IsDynkinDiagram n adj as: (1) adj.IsSymm, (2) no self-loops adj i i = 0, (3) adj i j ∈ {0,1}, (4) connectivity (path-connected), (5) positive definiteness of 2·Id - adj on ℤⁿ (x ≠ 0 → 0 < xᵀ(2·Id-adj)x). The book works over ℝ but positive definiteness over ℤ is equivalent here (integer vectors suffice for a lattice argument). All five conditions faithfully encode the book's definition of a Dynkin diagram.

Book: sα(v) = v - B(v,α)·α; simple reflections sᵢ = sαᵢ. Lean: rootReflection n A α v := v - (dotProduct v (A.mulVec α)) • α; simpleReflection n A i := rootReflection n A (Pi.single i 1). Both definitions are exact matches of the book formulas.

Book: 'A root is a nonzero vector x ∈ ℤⁿ such that B(x,x) = 2.' Lean: IsRoot n adj x := x ≠ 0 ∧ dotProduct x ((2 • 1 - adj).mulVec x) = 2. Exact match — (2·Id - adj) is the Cartan matrix, and dotProduct x (A.mulVec x) = B(x,x).
Book: 'αᵢ = (0,…,1,…,0) with 1 in position i.' Lean: simpleRoot n i := Pi.single i 1. Exact match — Pi.single i 1 is the standard basis vector eᵢ in ℤⁿ.

Book: 'A root α = Σᵢ kᵢ αᵢ is positive if all kᵢ ≥ 0; negative if all kᵢ ≤ 0.' Lean: IsPositiveRoot n adj x := IsRoot n adj x ∧ ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i; IsNegativeRoot n adj x := IsRoot n adj x ∧ ∀ i, x i ≤ 0. Since αᵢ are the standard basis vectors, the coordinates of x in the simple root basis are exactly x i. Faithful match.
